newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil co-ops report cold but no coffee frost.
newsitem.headline: Brazil co-ops report cold but no coffee frost.

text.p: Brazilian cooperative officials said they had not received any reports of frosts in coffee farms through Sunday morning despite very cold temperatures, particularly in the north of Parana state.
Regional weather service Simepar said temperatures had fallen to just below three degrees Celsius in some northern areas of Parana, with light frosts in low-lying areas where coffee is not grown.
Officials from local cooperatives in Londrina and Nova Londrina said there had been no reports of any problems from producers.
Temperatures were also very cold in southern Sao Paulo state, with the weather center in Presidente Prudente registering a low of five degrees Celsius.
But as in Parana, coffee-growing areas had seen no damaging cold, said the vice-president of the growers' National Coffee Council and president of the Garca cooperative in south Sao Paulo state.
"It was certainly cold but not so cold as to cause any problems," said Manoel Bertone.
The outlook is for further cold this evening although increasing cloud cover should protect most coffee regions, said local meteorologist Somar.

However highland areas such as Pocos de Caldas and Sao Sebastiao in Minas Gerais state could see a colder night than on Saturday/Sunday when minimum temperatures there were five to seven degrees Celsius.
"Temperatures could fall to around two to three degrees Celsius and there may be light frosts in lower-lying regions," said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
